text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu: defence budget should be increased.
- Israeli sources say Arafat wants to cause confrontation, thinks it will advance peace process.
- 60 cases of Hepatitis A in Arab village in Israel over last two years.
- Harry Woo, Chinese-American human rights activist: "From a moral standpoint, I don't understand Israel's position towards China".
JERUSALEM POST
- Seven Israeli crash victims still missing.
- Survivor Fuchs saved woman and baby.
- Palestinians lift Netzarim traffic blockade.
- PM's office: No new Golan settlements okayed.
- Police record-keeping is illegal, says court.
- *Western Wall on the web.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Little chance of finding survivors in Comoro crash.
- Education Ministry study: 40 percent of youngsters want a strong leader who won't have to rely on political parties or coalitions.
MAARIV
- Settlers threatening to block dozens of roads in West Bank, Gaza
- Lior Fuchs, Israeli survivor of Comoro crash: "A tragic end to an excellent vacation"
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel expected to lower prime rate today by 0.3 to 0.5 of percentage point
- Israel Aircraft Industry must receive bank approval before signing new deals
